name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  test:
    name: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          cache: npm

      - name: Audit dependencies
        run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=low

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Verify package signatures
        run: npm audit signatures

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Check formatting
        run: npm run format:check

      - name: Test
        run: npm test

      - name: Test CLI
        run: npm run test:cli

The Brotli fixture preserves `dist/node/main.js` from Markdown All in One 3.6.3.
Tests decompress and inspect the source without executing it. The accompanying
`markdown-all-in-one-LICENSE.txt` preserves the extension's distributed MIT license.

- Publisher and extension: `yzhang.markdown-all-in-one`, version `3.6.3`.
- Source: VS Code Marketplace, downloaded through the pinned clean-corpus manifest.
- Original VSIX SHA-256: `c4985b150497d430c3a7c884fd1f1ea7ed6de4846eb0192f8c770d9af8eb6e83`.
- Uncompressed source SHA-256: `9e351182a9d98bf1b3ba0b4bf5a08658e15147d4bd55596e8bf30b549145151b`.
- Uncompressed length: 1,533,214 bytes.
- The single U+202A is at UTF-16 offset 383,378, inside the KaTeX lexer class
  `[!-\\[\\]-‧<U+202A>-퟿豈-￿]`.

The exception covers only that character in that exact source. Renaming a file cannot
create an exception. Editing, prefixing, or appending source invalidates the hash.
New bundle versions require a fresh review and an independently verified source hash.

To reproduce the compressed fixture from the verified source, use Node's
`brotliCompressSync` with `BROTLI_PARAM_QUALITY` set to `11`. Decompression must restore
both the source length and SHA-256 listed above.

name: Docker

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  release:
    types: [published]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: docker-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  test:
    name: Docker (${{ matrix.platform }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04
            platform: linux/amd64
            arch: amd64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            platform: linux/arm64
            arch: arm64
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1

      - name: Build image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: ${{ matrix.platform }}
          load: true
          tags: vsix-audit:test
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=docker-${{ matrix.arch }}
          cache-to: type=gha,scope=docker-${{ matrix.arch }},mode=max

      - name: Test image
        run: node scripts/test-docker.mjs vsix-audit:test

  publish:
    name: Publish Docker image
    needs: test
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write # Publish the tested image to GitHub Container Registry.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@99012661954931238ded8c8b007157a8430204e1 # v4.4.0
        with:
          platforms: arm64

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1

      - name: Image tags and labels
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@dc802804100637a589fabce1cb79ff13a1411302 # v6.2.0
        env:
          STABLE_RELEASE: >-
            ${{ github.event_name == 'release' && !github.event.release.prerelease }}
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
          flavor: latest=false
          tags: |
            type=raw,value=main,enable=${{ github.event_name == 'push' }}
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ env.STABLE_RELEASE }}

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@81c6f93d4bc991e510b342a00b419b3bb4efc5c6 # v4.7.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Publish image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          provenance: mode=max
          sbom: true
          cache-from: |
            type=gha,scope=docker-amd64
            type=gha,scope=docker-arm64

name: Publish to npm

on:
  release:
    types: [published]

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write # Required for OIDC trusted publishing
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
          package-manager-cache: false

      - run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=low

      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
      - run: npm audit signatures
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npm publish --provenance --access public

# vsix-audit

Security scanner for VS Code extensions. Detects malicious extensions before installation by analyzing code patterns, indicators of compromise, and known malware signatures.

## The Problem

VS Code extensions run with full trust and the same permissions as the editor itself. Malicious extensions have been found in both the official Microsoft marketplace and OpenVSX:

- **Credential theft** - SSH keys, browser cookies, password manager databases
- **Cryptocurrency theft** - Wallet files, clipboard hijacking for addresses
- **Source code exfiltration** - Stealing proprietary code via Discord webhooks
- **Cryptominers and RATs** - CoinIMP miners, ScreenConnect RATs, multi-stage loaders
- **Self-propagation** - GlassWorm spread by modifying installed extensions

## Detection Modules

The scanner runs nine detection modules by default. Add `--check-repository` for source
repository checks over GitHub's API. Select individual checks with `--module`, for
example `--module manifest,execution,deps,intel` for package and execution analysis.

### Manifest, Execution, Dependency, And Intel Analysis (`package.ts`)

Examines `package.json`, extension manifest behavior, runtime execution patterns, and
package-related threat intelligence.

| Check                  | What It Detects                                                                 | Severity        |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| Blocklist              | Extension ID matches known malicious extensions                                 | Critical        |
| Wildcard activation    | `activationEvents: ["*"]` - runs on every action                                | High            |
| Startup activation     | `onStartupFinished` - runs at VS Code launch                                    | Medium          |
| Theme with code        | Theme extension that has a `main` entry point                                   | High            |
| Malicious npm packages | Dependencies matching known malware package names                               | Critical        |
| Malicious npm versions | Resolved/bundled dependency versions matching known compromised releases        | Critical        |
| Typosquatting          | Dependencies within edit distance 1-2 of popular packages (lodash, axios, etc.) | High            |
| Lifecycle scripts      | `preinstall`/`postinstall` scripts with suspicious patterns                     | Critical/Medium |
| Hidden task execution  | VS Code tasks executed with suppressed task UI                                  | High            |
| GitHub SHA execution   | `npx`/`npm exec` against `github:owner/repo#sha`                                | Critical        |
| Startup execution      | `onStartupFinished` paired with task/process launch behavior                    | High            |

### Indicators of Compromise (`ioc.ts`)

Matches against curated threat intelligence from `zoo/iocs/`.

| Check          | Detection Method                                                    | Severity |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| Malware hashes | SHA256 hash of files matches known samples                          | Critical |
| C2 domains     | Domain extraction matched against blocklist                         | Critical |
| C2 IPs         | IPv4 extraction (excludes private ranges) matched against blocklist | Critical |
| GitHub C2      | GitHub API/raw URLs referencing known C2 accounts                   | Critical |
| Crypto wallets | BTC (legacy/SegWit/Bech32), ETH, Monero, Solana address patterns    | High     |

### AST Analysis (`ast.ts`)

OXC-based parsing to detect structural patterns that regex can't catch.

| Rule                       | What It Detects                                  | Severity |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------- |
| `AST_EVAL_DYNAMIC`         | `eval(variable)` - non-literal argument          | High     |
| `AST_FUNCTION_CONSTRUCTOR` | `new Function(string)` - runtime code generation | High     |
| `AST_DYNAMIC_REQUIRE`      | `require(variable)` - computed module loads      | Medium   |
| `AST_DYNAMIC_IMPORT`       | `import(variable)` - computed dynamic imports    | Medium   |
| `AST_PROCESS_BINDING`      | `process.binding()` - Node.js internals access   | High     |
| `AST_GLOBAL_THIS_EVAL`     | `globalThis.eval` - indirect eval access         | High     |

### Obfuscation Detection (`obfuscation.ts`)

Detects obfuscation techniques used to hide malicious intent.

| Rule                       | Detection Method                                                  | Severity |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `OBFUSCATION_HIGH_ENTROPY` | Shannon entropy >5.5 bits/char (200-char windows)                 | Medium   |
| `ZERO_WIDTH_CHARS`         | Zero-width spaces/joiners hiding code (U+200B-200D)               | High     |
| `VARIATION_SELECTOR`       | GlassWorm-style hidden data in variation selectors (U+FE00-FE0F)  | Critical |
| `BIDI_OVERRIDE`            | Trojan Source attacks using bidirectional overrides (U+202A-202E) | Critical |
| `UNICODE_ASCII_ESCAPE`     | `\u00XX` escapes for normal ASCII chars (obfuscation)             | Medium   |
| `CYRILLIC_HOMOGLYPH`       | Cyrillic letters that look like Latin (а/a, е/e, с/c)             | High     |
| `OTHER_INVISIBLE_CHARS`    | Soft hyphens, combining marks, format controls                    | Medium   |
| `INVISIBLE_CODE_EXECUTION` | Invisible chars near `eval`/`Function`/`exec`                     | Critical |

JavaScript obfuscation patterns (hex variables, `fromCharCode` arrays, eval+decode, packers) are now detected via YARA rules for better accuracy.

The Unicode check exempts U+202A only at validated range endpoints in regex literals and
at one known KaTeX lexer position in the exact Markdown All in One 3.6.3 source bundle.
The KaTeX exception requires the full source SHA-256 and character offset recorded in
`bidi-ranges.ts`; any source edit invalidates it. Other regex constructor strings remain
reportable. The [fixture provenance](src/scanner/checks/fixtures/README.md) documents the
verified artifact and offline regression fixture.

### YARA Rules (`yara.ts`)

External YARA-X engine for complex pattern matching. Rules loaded from `zoo/signatures/yara/`. Requires `yr` CLI (`brew install yara-x`).

| Rule File                     | Detects                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `blockchain_c2.yar`           | Solana RPC C2, memo parsing, blockchain-based command channels |
| `blockchain_c2_extended.yar`  | Ethereum smart contract C2 via ethers.js                       |
| `code_execution.yar`          | `eval`, `Function` constructor, `child_process` patterns       |
| `credential_harvesting.yar`   | NPM/GitHub/SSH credential theft, `.npmrc` access               |
| `crypto_wallet_targeting.yar` | MetaMask, Phantom, Exodus wallet extension targeting           |
| `data_exfiltration.yar`       | Discord webhooks, SSH key theft, browser data exfil            |
| `google_calendar_c2.yar`      | Google Calendar API abuse for C2 communication                 |
| `multi_stage_attacks.yar`     | Dropper chains, reverse shells, keylogger patterns             |
| `native_addon_loader.yar`     | Suspicious .node native addon loading patterns                 |
| `obfuscation_patterns.yar`    | Hex variables, `fromCharCode`, packed/encoded code             |
| `persistence_macos.yar`       | LaunchAgent persistence, Apple masquerading, Login Items       |
| `powershell_attacks.yar`      | Hidden windows, `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`, AMSI evasion        |
| `rat_capabilities.yar`        | SOCKS proxy, VNC, remote command execution                     |
| `rmm_tool_delivery.yar`       | ScreenConnect, AnyDesk, TeamViewer delivery via extensions     |
| `self_propagation.yar`        | GlassWorm-style worm propagation via extension modification    |
| `unicode_stealth.yar`         | Invisible Unicode, variation selectors, homoglyphs             |

### Telemetry Detection (`telemetry.ts`)

Reports references to external analytics, crash-reporting, and application performance
monitoring services. Static references do not establish that a request executes.

| Check           | What It Detects                                                   | Severity      |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| SDK imports     | Known telemetry packages (Sentry, Mixpanel, PostHog, AppInsights) | High          |
| Endpoint URLs   | URLs matching known telemetry services from `zoo/telemetry/`      | High          |
| Telemetry paths | API paths like `/collect`, `/track`, `/ingest`, `/metrics`        | High          |
| Data collection | Patterns near telemetry code (machine_id, user_id, file_paths)    | Informational |

The report records telemetry settings and `isTelemetryEnabled` references as hints.
It marks opt-out enforcement as unverified and retains the finding severity. A reference
in a comment, unused setting, or unrelated file cannot establish that telemetry respects
user preferences.

### Triage-Friendly Output

Every finding includes context to help quickly determine if it's a real threat:

- **Legitimate uses** - Why this pattern exists in benign extensions
- **Red flags** - What makes the same pattern suspicious in context
- **Severity** - Critical/high/medium/low based on risk and intent signals
- **Location** - File path and line number for the match

The goal is rich context for human/agent review, not just pass/fail.

## Installation

```sh
brew install yara-x
npm install -g @trailofbits/vsix-audit
```

Requires Node.js 24 or later and [YARA-X](https://github.com/VirusTotal/yara-x) for YARA rule scanning.

### Docker

The Docker image includes Node.js, YARA-X, and the bundled detection data. Images support
Linux amd64 and arm64 and run as the unprivileged `node` user (UID 1000).

Scan a local extension by mounting its directory read-only:

```sh
docker run --rm \
  --mount type=bind,src="$(pwd)",dst=/work,readonly \
  ghcr.io/trailofbits/vsix-audit:main scan ./extension.vsix
```

Scan a marketplace extension without a local mount:

```sh
docker run --rm ghcr.io/trailofbits/vsix-audit:main scan ms-python.python
```

To scan installed extensions, mount the host's extension store and pass its container path:

```sh
docker run --rm \
  --mount type=bind,src="$HOME/.vscode/extensions",dst=/extensions,readonly \
  ghcr.io/trailofbits/vsix-audit:main scan-installed --extensions-dir /extensions
```

All CLI options are available after the image name. Exit codes are preserved: `0` for no
findings, `1` for findings, and `2` for an error or required coverage failure. For example,
append `--output json --strict --require-yara` to produce JSON and require complete coverage.
For offline local scans, add Docker's `--network none` before the image name.

The `main` tag follows the default branch. Stable releases also publish `latest` and a
version tag, such as `0.4.0`; prereleases publish only their version tag.

Build and test the image locally:

```sh
docker build -t vsix-audit:test .
npm run test:docker
```

## Usage

### Commands

**Scan an extension for security issues:**

```sh
vsix-audit scan ./extension.vsix
vsix-audit scan publisher.extension-name
vsix-audit scan openvsx:publisher/extension-name
```

**Scan installed extensions:**

```sh
vsix-audit scan-installed
vsix-audit scan-installed --editor cursor
vsix-audit scan-installed --editor vscode --output json
vsix-audit scan-installed --extensions-dir ./portable/data/extensions --strict
```

`scan-installed` scans the default user extension stores for VS Code, VS Code Insiders,
and Cursor. It reads extension files directly without launching an editor or activating extensions.
Every version on disk is scanned, including disabled extensions and leftover versions.

| Editor          | Default store                   |
| --------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `vscode`        | `~/.vscode/extensions`          |
| `insiders`      | `~/.vscode-insiders/extensions` |
| `cursor`        | `~/.cursor/extensions`          |
| `all` (default) | All three stores that exist     |

On Windows, `~` means the current user's home directory, normally `%USERPROFILE%`.
Use `--extensions-dir <path>` for custom, portable, or remote extension stores mounted locally,
or for editor settings that this process cannot see. This option cannot be combined with `--editor`.
For VS Code and Insiders, discovery follows [VS Code's][vscode-extensions]
path precedence: `--extensions-dir`, `VSCODE_EXTENSIONS`, `VSCODE_PORTABLE` plus `/extensions`,
then the default store. Cursor uses its own default store unless `--extensions-dir` is given.
Directories reached through multiple symbolic links are scanned once.

The command accepts the output, severity, module, threat-intelligence, profiling, and coverage
options below, plus `--jobs <n>` (default: 4). JSON results include each directory in
`metadata.sourcePath`; SARIF findings use absolute file URIs to distinguish editor stores.
Text, JSON, and SARIF reports record the searched roots and the inventory scope. Discovery
does not identify the active profile or enumerate remote hosts. `--profile` reports scan
timings. It does not select a VS Code profile.
Missing default stores are skipped. An empty inventory, an unreadable store, or any failed
extension scan returns exit code `2`. Broken extension links and unreadable stores are retained
as errors while healthy targets continue scanning. Partial reports include both results and errors.

**Download an extension for offline analysis:**

```sh
vsix-audit download ms-python.python
vsix-audit download ms-python.python@2024.1.0 -o ./downloads
vsix-audit download openvsx:redhat/java
```

**Show extension metadata:**

```sh
vsix-audit info ./extension.vsix
vsix-audit info ./extension-folder
```

Displays: name, publisher, version, activation events, entry points, contributions, dependencies, file count, and size.

### Registry Prefixes

| Prefix         | Registry                       |
| -------------- | ------------------------------ |
| (none)         | VS Code Marketplace (default)  |
| `marketplace:` | VS Code Marketplace (explicit) |
| `openvsx:`     | Open VSX Registry              |

### Scan Options

| Option                   | Description                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-o, --output <format>`  | Output format: `text`, `json`, or `sarif` (default: `text`)                      |
| `-s, --severity <level>` | Minimum severity to report: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical` (default: `low`) |
| `-m, --module <names>`   | Comma-separated detection modules to run                                         |
| `-r, --recursive`        | Recursively scan all .vsix files in a directory                                  |
| `-j, --jobs <n>`         | Number of parallel scans (default: 4, used with --recursive)                     |
| `--no-cache`             | Bypass cache, download fresh                                                     |
| `--force`                | Re-download even if cached                                                       |
| `--all-registries`       | Scan from all registries (Marketplace + OpenVSX + Cursor)                        |
| `--threat-intel <mode>`  | Threat intelligence mode: `local` or `none` (default: `local`)                   |
| `--no-threat-intel`      | Disable threat-intelligence datasets while keeping generic detections            |
| `--strict`               | Exit with an error if scan coverage is degraded                                  |
| `--require-yara`         | Exit with an error if YARA scanning cannot run                                   |
| `--check-repository`     | Check declared GitHub source repositories over the network                       |

### Repository Checks

```bash
vsix-audit scan publisher.extension-name --check-repository
vsix-audit scan ./extension.vsix --module repository
```

Repository checks read the root `package.json` repository field and the VSIX metadata
properties `Microsoft.VisualStudio.Services.Links.Source` and
`Microsoft.VisualStudio.Services.Links.GitHub`. They support GitHub web links, Git URLs,
and npm's GitHub shorthand. Other hosts remain unverified. Default scans stay offline
after any requested extension download.

Missing links, inaccessible repositories or owners, and repositories with no commits
produce low-severity findings. A repository may be private, and source disclosure is
optional. These observations do not establish that an extension is malicious.

Timeouts, rate limits, malformed metadata, and unsupported hosts produce coverage warnings.
Use `--strict` to require a completed repository check. Set `GITHUB_TOKEN` to authenticate
GitHub API requests; its permissions determine which private repositories can be checked.
Requests have time and response-size limits, follow redirects within supported GitHub API
endpoints, and share bounded lookups within a batch. Rate-limited batches stop sending requests.

### Coverage Degradation

`vsix-audit` reports incomplete work in `metadata.coverage`, independently of the
minimum severity selected for findings. `incompleteModules` names checks that failed or
could not finish. Empty or invalid YARA rules, parser recovery errors, skipped input
files, and missing entry points degrade coverage. `--require-yara` returns exit code `2`
when YARA coverage is incomplete. Missing detection datasets fail with a named error;
required data never silently becomes an empty dataset.

Directory scans include bundled dependencies and apply the archive entry-point and size
checks, including files inside `.git` directories. Symbolic links and special files inside
an extension are skipped with a coverage warning. The scanner reads extension contents without
executing them.

Known network indicators are checked regardless of filename or binary format. YARA retains
its script-oriented format filters and 10 MiB file limit. Native libraries, executables,
WebAssembly, and other recognized compiled formats produce coverage warnings because the
script analyzers cannot inspect their behavior. `--strict` fails on these limits even when
indicator checks find no threats. `--require-yara` also fails when YARA skips a compiled
format. Inspect these files with tools for their executable format.

SARIF retains coverage warnings as tool execution notifications and marks incomplete
invocations unsuccessful. YARA findings include up to 20 string excerpts and their byte
offsets in JSON and SARIF, plus the total match count. Text reports show the first five.
YARA output is streamed so repeated matches cannot exhaust an output buffer. The YARA process
has a 60-second deadline; timeouts produce a coverage failure while retaining completed records.
YARA text locations include one-based lines and UTF-16 columns. Binary evidence uses byte
offsets. Terminal reports escape controls in untrusted text; JSON and SARIF preserve the
original values through JSON escapes.

Generated and dependency paths receive the same detection checks. Unicode exceptions
use validated regex ranges, the pinned KaTeX occurrence, and local emoji or Arabic
joining context. Filenames cannot exempt directional controls.

Use `--strict` for production gating when an incomplete scan should fail closed. Use `--require-yara` when YARA coverage is mandatory in CI.

### Extension Cache

Downloaded extensions are cached for faster subsequent scans:

| Platform | Cache Location                                          |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| macOS    | `~/Library/Caches/vsix-audit/`                          |
| Linux    | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/vsix-audit/` or `~/.cache/vsix-audit/` |

Extensions are organized by registry (`marketplace/`, `openvsx/`, `cursor/`).

Set `VSIX_AUDIT_CACHE_DIR` to override the cache location, which is useful for CI and sandboxed environments.

**Cache management commands:**

```sh
vsix-audit cache path              # Print cache directory
vsix-audit cache list [--json]     # List cached extensions
vsix-audit cache clear [pattern]   # Clear cache (optional glob pattern)
vsix-audit cache info <ext-id>     # Show cached versions
```

**Examples:**

```sh
# First scan downloads to cache
vsix-audit scan ms-python.python
# → Downloaded ~/.cache/vsix-audit/marketplace/ms-python.python-2024.1.0.vsix

# Second scan uses cache
vsix-audit scan ms-python.python
# → Using cached ~/.cache/vsix-audit/marketplace/ms-python.python-2024.1.0.vsix

# Force re-download
vsix-audit scan --force ms-python.python

# Bypass cache entirely
vsix-audit scan --no-cache ms-python.python

# Clear specific extensions
vsix-audit cache clear ms-python.*
```

`scan --no-cache` downloads to a temporary directory and removes it when the scan
finishes or fails. `download --no-cache` saves the VSIX to the current directory,
or to the directory selected with `--output`. Neither command reads or writes the
persistent cache in this mode. Use `scan --force` to download fresh and update the cache.
New downloads replace the destination after the transfer completes, so an interrupted
transfer preserves an existing file.

### Output Formats

**Text** (default) - Human-readable report for terminal output.

**JSON** - Machine-readable results for integration with other tools.

**SARIF** - Static Analysis Results Interchange Format for CI/CD integration.

### Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning           |
| ---- | ----------------- |
| 0    | No findings       |
| 1    | Findings detected |
| 2    | Error during scan |

In `--strict` mode, exit code `2` is also used for degraded scanner coverage. With `--require-yara`, exit code `2` is used when YARA scanning cannot run.

Batch scans return `2` if any target fails, even when other extensions scan successfully or
have findings. `--all-registries` uses the same JSON batch result and SARIF error reporting
as directory scans. Missing registry entries, download errors, and scan failures remain
visible alongside successful results.

### Benign False-Positive Corpus

Pinned benign extension metadata lives in `test-corpus/clean/manifest.json`. The VSIX files are downloaded locally and ignored by git.

```bash
# Download pinned clean corpus artifacts and verify SHA-256 hashes
npm run corpus:download

# Scan the local clean corpus
vsix-audit scan test-corpus/clean --recursive

# Generate a false-positive report
npm run corpus:report

# Fail if any never-in-clean findings appear
npm run corpus:check
```

# YARA Rules for VS Code Extension Malware

Detection signatures for scanning extensions.

## External Rules

We recommend using the Knostic GlassWorm YARA rules:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/knostic/open-tools.git
cp open-tools/glassworm_yara/*.yar zoo/signatures/yara/
```

### Knostic Rule Files

| ----------------------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `unicode_stealth.yar`         | 2     | Invisible Unicode characters, zero-width obfuscation |
| `blockchain_c2.yar`           | 3     | Solana RPC C2, memo field parsing                    |
| `credential_harvesting.yar`   | 5     | NPM/GitHub/OpenVSX/SSH credential theft              |
| `google_calendar_c2.yar`      | 4     | Calendar API abuse for C2                            |

Source: https://github.com/knostic/open-tools/tree/main/glassworm_yara

## Custom Rules

Add custom YARA rules to this directory. Follow naming convention:

```
{campaign}_{detection_type}.yar
```

Example: `tigerjack_keylogger.yar`

## Usage

```bash
# Scan with YARA-X
yr scan -r zoo/signatures/yara/unicode_stealth.yar path/to/extension/

# Or scan all rules in directory
for f in zoo/signatures/yara/*.yar; do yr scan -r "$f" path/to/extension/; done

# With vsix-audit (automatic)
vsix-audit scan extension.vsix  # YARA rules loaded automatically
```

## Rule metadata

Rules declare `severity` (`low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`) and a description.
Optional `capabilities` lists `network`, `execution`, `fileAccess`, `credentials`, or
`obfuscation`, separated by commas. The scanner reads these fields from YARA-X output.

The eval/Base64, eval/character-construction, obfuscation/eval, download/write/execute,
credential-file exfiltration, and remote-execution rules report medium-severity advisory
references. Their matches do not establish a data-flow relationship between the strings.
Verified clean bundles contain these combinations too; generated or dependency paths
receive the same checks.
The clean-corpus guard rejects every critical finding, including findings from new rules.
